clue.text: Grouse about initial radio transmission of space

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole run of pieces that follows is read backwards

parts.note: LW, the initials of long wave, a band of radio transmission
taken as written
a room is a space

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the first broadcast sent out from space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run round at once, giving MOORFOWL. 'Grouse' looks like a complaint but is the bird being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse is a game bird of the moors, so it is a kind of moor-dwelling fowl.

clue.text: Author detailed gnome to replace music maker

indicators.note: to re-place the letters is to put them back in new positions, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the final letter, cut off

explanation.surface: A writer's garden gnome is swapped for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the E from GNOME, giving GNOM; 'to replace' then shuffles AUTHOR plus GNOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica, the small instrument blown across the lips, is something that makes music.

clue.text: Ignored while being in full view

definitions.meaning: missed or passed over without notice
looked down on from above, as a garden is by a neighbour's windows

explanation.surface: Someone was passed over even though they were standing in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both failing to notice something and being visible from a higher place.

clue.text: Soccer's over for American spies at the front

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits over, that is above, the next

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, governing soccer in England
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A football match is finished, so the American agents go to the frontline.
explanation.walkthrough: FA above CIA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A facia (fascia) is the board across a shop front, so it is a front.

clue.text: An endowment of sophisticated commodities?

parts.note: worldly means experienced and sophisticated
goods are commodities, things for sale

explanation.surface: A gift of refined merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions are what a person is endowed with, an endowment of material things.

clue.text: Know-how, when University replaces Tech, is inimitable

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means substituting it in the word

parts.note: technique is skill or know-how

explanation.surface: A college's expertise is unmatched once it stops being a technical college.
explanation.walkthrough: In TECHNIQUE, U (University) replaces TECH, as the clue spells out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one of a kind cannot be copied, which is what inimitable says.

clue.text: Pennons or switches for a has-been

indicators.note: switches signals the letters swap places into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Flags are swapped about for a faded celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A person treated as no longer existing or mattering is a has-been, a figure of no account.

clue.text: Curious TV show?

definitions.meaning: an old sense of the word as a verb is to look at curiously or quizzically

explanation.surface: An odd television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a television question contest, and in old use means to eye with curiosity.

clue.text: We're told to manipulate the creatures

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: to use someone is to manipulate them

explanation.surface: We have been instructed to handle the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so they are creatures.

clue.text: Not yet ready for the scrapheap, but are they being exploited?

definitions.text: Not yet ready for the scrapheap, but are they being exploited?

parts.words: Not yet ready for the scrapheap, but are they being exploited?
parts.note: second-hand motors still roadworthy, with a play on vehicles that have been used and so exploited

explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand vehicles are not yet scrap, and have been put to use, hence exploited.

clue.text: Intricately veined salad plant

indicators.note: intricately signals the letters woven into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A salad leaf with a complex network of veins.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy plant, related to chicory, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Copy, including rewritten score, is of a small movement

indicators.note: including means one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: to mimic is to copy

indicators.note: rewritten signals the letters are written out again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A copy of a musical score, revised, depicts a little piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' gives CROSE from the fodder. 'Movement' looks musical but is the earth shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Microseismic describes a tiny earth tremor, a small movement of the ground.

clue.text: Lines for article in carrier with first class directions for making sauce

indicators.note: the clue words that say one part holds the other

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
an is the indefinite article
A1 means first class, written AI
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: Recipe instructions for a sauce, involving lines, articles and a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is the open trough a hodman carries bricks in on the shoulder; A1 is a traditional mark of top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollandaise is a rich butter and egg-yolk sauce served with fish or eggs.

clue.text: Romp home with such a bun in Sussex

parts.note: to romp home is to win easily
a Chelsea bun is a currant-filled rolled bun

explanation.surface: Win easily and celebrate with a sticky bun in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in southern England; Winchelsea is a small town there. The definition says where the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchelsea is an old town in East Sussex, so it is something found in that county.

clue.text: He's with egghead outside painting the Deep Pansy

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
painting is a form of art
the deep is a poetic name for the sea
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A man, together with an intellectual, is out painting a dark pansy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the painting and the sea within HE'S. 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but supplies only its head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is the wild pansy, a small violet-like flower.

clue.text: Goes bad with nothing in the undergrowth

indicators.note: in places the nought inside the other word

parts.note: food that goes bad rots
O, the figure nought, is nothing

explanation.surface: Something decays with nothing left in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant roots grow underneath, read playfully as the growth that is under the ground.

clue.text: Point to listener with child at home, good but inquisitive

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the ear is the organ of listening
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone points at a listener while a well-behaved child stays home, yet is nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A searching look or question probes deeply, so it is inquisitive.

clue.text: Two monarchs giving sovereign's first greeting in long ago county

indicators.note: in puts this run of pieces inside the old word

parts.note: yore means time long ago
R (rex) and K (king) are two abbreviations for a monarch
R (rex) and K (king) are two abbreviations for a monarch

indicators.note: first means taking only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Two kings and a sovereign exchange greetings in an old county.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a large county in northern England. R (rex) and K (king) are the usual monarch abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is a historic English county, the largest in Britain.

clue.text: He loves me … he loves me not … now nothing's left!

definitions.text: He loves me … he loves me not … now nothing's left!

parts.words: He loves me … he loves me not … now nothing's left!
parts.note: the daisy game of plucking petals one by one until the flower has none left

explanation.definitionFit: Apetalous means having no petals, as a daisy is once every petal is plucked away.

clue.text: Check back about note being more agreeable

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the note
back means read in reverse

parts.note: to rein in is to check
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Checking back on a note to find a pleasanter tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REIN into NIER, and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Theologian, one in the money, on the point of displaying ungentlemanly behaviour

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after
in puts the theologian and one inside the money

parts.note: cash is money
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A rich divine on the brink of behaving like a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means the headland comes after. A cad is an old word for a man who behaves badly towards others.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, so caddishness is ungentlemanly conduct.

clue.text: Well-shod, she (or he, perhaps) might be a winner

definitions.text: Well-shod, she (or he, perhaps) might be a winner

parts.words: Well-shod, she (or he, perhaps) might be a winner
parts.note: an animal fitted with iron shoes, mare or stallion, that might win a race

explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses wear shoes, can be mares or stallions, and run to win.

clue.text: Saying expert ignored part of speech

indicators.note: ignored means the expert is left out of the word

parts.note: a proverb is a saying
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert's saying overlooked a grammatical point.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbs, like nouns and adjectives, are one of the grammatical word classes.

clue.text: Spirits or joint over the pub?

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over the next

parts.note: J is slang for a cannabis joint
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A choice between drinks or a smoke above the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like drink but means supernatural beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are spirits of Arabian and Islamic lore, also called genies.

clue.text: Team in anger rejected the potion

indicators.note: in places the team inside the reversed word
rejected means thrown back, so read in reverse

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A team angrily turned down the magic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the word for anger round, giving ELIR. XI is eleven, the size of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical or medicinal drink, a potion.

clue.text: A doctor gets run out to South Africa, taking in fabulous food

annotationWithheld.clue: A doctor gets run out to South Africa, taking in fabulous food

clue.text: Live number, it's said. Gracious!

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: to live is to be, and nine is a number

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a live music number.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and gentle, much as gracious does.

clue.text: Trapped in a glacier, a teetotaller appears to turn to steel

indicators.note: trapped in means the letters sit concealed within these words

explanation.surface: A non-drinker frozen in a glacier seems to become steel.
explanation.definitionFit: To acierate is to convert iron into steel.
